---
title: "Research"
---

I use empirical data and mathematical models to investigate how evolution shapes biological diversity. My current work spans two areas: the macroevolution of morphological complexity in marine bivalves and the population genetics of linked selection.

## Morphological complexity and macroevolution

### How does morphological complexity vary across latitude?

I developed a measure of shell ornamentation complexity to compare morphological and taxonomic patterns across marine bivalves in the West Pacific and West Atlantic. Our results show that species richness and shell complexity follow different latitudinal patterns. By separating changes in species composition within and among families, I investigate how these patterns are assembled and how they relate to ecology.

In earlier work, we showed that ecological functions did not accumulate in an early burst relative to taxonomic diversity during the initial evolution of bivalves ([Zhou et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsbl.2023.0157)). Together, these studies ask how different aspects of biodiversity follow different evolutionary trajectories.

An emerging direction is to investigate how morphological diversity is assembled and maintained through time, including how the variation lineages can produce interacts with ecological conditions and differential survival.

*Advisor: [David Jablonski](https://geosci.uchicago.edu/people/david-jablonski/)*


## Generative models of shell ornamentation

### How does development shape the paths of morphological evolution?

I develop generative models of bivalve shell ornamentation to investigate how growth processes shape the variation available to evolution. My goal is to map how changes in underlying growth processes translate into changes in shell form, generating predictions about developmental accessibility—which morphological transitions are more likely under the model. By comparing these predictions with morphological transitions inferred from phylogenies, I aim to test whether development helps explain which changes recur across evolutionary lineages, and where observed evolution departs from the model's predictions.

*Advisor: [David Jablonski](https://geosci.uchicago.edu/people/david-jablonski/)*


## Impact of linked stabilizing selection on genetic diversity

### How does stabilizing selection on complex traits shape genetic diversity?

Models of pleiotropic stabilizing selection help explain patterns of genetic variation in many human complex traits. I develop population-genetic theory to ask what this implies for genetic diversity at linked sites. We find that, in the regimes studied, our model of stabilizing selection produces greater reductions in linked neutral diversity than purifying selection with the same heterozygote fitness cost. I am applying this framework to human traits such as height, using estimates of genetic architecture to predict the effects of pleiotropic stabilizing selection on linked neutral diversity.

*Work with: [Jeremy Berg](http://www.jjbpopgen.org/)*
